labels.label: ex:following_example_skeletal_itemize

hypotheses.paper: item 3: pure n-dimensional simplicial complex, k <= n-2
hypotheses.note: finite complex, locally strongly connected in codimension >= 2 (GX.IsLocallyStronglyConnected); without it the item is false (GX.bowtie_counterexample)
n >= 2 (finrank >= 2); in dimension 1 the item fails (GX.eq_empty_of_isSkeletal_real); 'wildly' presupposes n >= 3 anyway

findings: Item 3 (l.372) is false as written: the bow-tie (two triangles sharing a vertex) is a pure 2-complex whose 0-skeleton is not skeletal (GX.bowtie_counterexample, pre-existing). With local strong connectivity in codimension >= 2 added, the corrected statement is now proved in full (no sorry).
questions: Item 2 read as a closed locally flat subset (pre-existing reading, unchanged by this package).

kb_proposals: Non-separation by closed totally disconnected sets needs no dimension theory: Janiszewski's lemma for disjoint closed sets follows from lifting C(Y, ℂ∖{0}) through exp on a simply connected Y (Complex.isCoveringMapOn_exp.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts), and a Zorn argument on minimal separating closed sets reduces to points (GX.isPreconnected_compl_of_separated).

A closed subset of a finite-dimensional space is locally compact, so totally disconnected = totally separated there (loc_compact_t2_tot_disc_iff_tot_sep): clopen splits of non-compact closed sets are available.

Local theory of geometric simplicial complexes without carriers: GX.openSimplex (positive barycentric weights) + AffineIndependent.eq_of_sum_eq_sum_subtype gives 'a point of the open simplex of a face lies only in faces containing it'; open stars are replaced by B(x,r) ∩ {y | every face through y passes through x}, open because K is finite.
notes: Both tagged sorries of GXScaffold.Topology.PortlyExamples are closed; the statements of GX.isPreconnected_compl_of_isTotallyDisconnected and GX.isSkeletal_skeletonSpace_codim_two are byte-identical to the dispatch's.
